He is one of India's richest people according to [[Forbes]]. Singh was the chairman and [[chief executive officer]] of the Indian real estate company [[DLF Limited|DLF]], founded by his father-in-law [[Chaudhary Raghvendra Singh]], until 2020.{{cite web|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/leisure/story/20111128-whatever-the-odds-the-incredible-story-behind-dlf-by-kpsingh-749727-2011-11-18|title=The trials and triumphs of K.P. Singh : Leisure|work=India Today|date=18 November 2011 |access-date=2 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001052946/https://indiatoday.intoday.in/story/whatever-the-odds-the-incredible-story-behind-dlf-by-k.p.singh/1/160593.html|archive-date=1 October 2015|url-status=live}}{{cite web|url=https://www.dlf.in|title=DLF|publisher=Dlf.in|access-date=2 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060331032441/http://www.dlf.in/|archive-date=31 March 2006|url-status=live}} Singh built DLF into the largest real estate company in India and DLF holds India's largest [[Land banking|land bank]] of more than 10,000 acres.{{Cite web |last=Chadha |first=Sunainaa |date=9 May 2024 |title=NRIs galore: DLF sells 795 flats priced at Rs 7 cr in Gurugram in 3 days |url=https://www.business-standard.com/finance/personal-finance/nris-galore-dlf-sells-795-flats-priced-at-rs-7-cr-in-gurugram-in-3-days-124050900234_1.html |access-date=13 January 2025 |website=Business Standard |archive-date=16 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240516160748/https://www.business-standard.com/finance/personal-finance/nris-galore-dlf-sells-795-flats-priced-at-rs-7-cr-in-gurugram-in-3-days-124050900234_1.html |url-status=live }} His autobiography, named ''Whatever the Odds: The Incredible Story Behind DLF'', was published in 2011; [[Jack Welch]] spoke at the launch.{{cite web |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/north/story/delhi-autobiography-of-dlf-chairman-k-p-singh-launched-145848-2011-11-14 |title=DLF Chairman K. P. Singh's autobiography launched in Delhi : North, News |website=India Today |date=15 November 2011 |access-date=5 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160116003727/http://indiatoday.intoday.in/story/delhi-autobiography-of-dlf-chairman-k.-p.-singh-launched/1/160078.html |archive-date=16 January 2016 |url-status=live }} Singh has been noted for making [[Gurgaon]], [[Haryana]], from a village into a modern and developed city. Singh has also been noted for his relationship with the [[Nehru–Gandhi family|Nehru-Gandhi]] [[political family]], which, according to him, benefited his businesses especially during its early stages, and has also been a source of controversy during his career. In October 2024, Singh was ranked 12th on the ''Forbes'' list of India's 100 richest, with a net worth of $20.5 billion.{{Cite web |date=October 9, 2024 |title=India's 100 Richest |url=https://www.forbes.com/lists/india-billionaires/ |website=India’s 100 Richest |access-date=15 October 2024 |archive-date=3 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241103210346/https://www.forbes.com/lists/india-billionaires/ |url-status=live }} == Early life and military career == Kushal Pal Singh was born on 15 August 1931 to a family of [[Jats|Jat]] landlords{{cite book |last1=Singh |first1=K. P. (Kushal Pal) |url=https://archive.org/details/whateveroddsincr0000sing/page/88/mode/2up?q=Jat+origins |title=Whatever the odds : the incredible story behind DLF |date=2011 |publisher=New Delhi : HarperCollins Publishers India, a joint venture with The India Today Group |isbn=978-93-5029-134-4 |page=88 |quote=My Jat origins and family were to come to my rescue on another occasion, this time in a rather bizarre incident}}{{Cite magazine |last=Robinson |first=Simon |date=2007-08-02 |title=60 Years of Independence - TIME |url=https://content.time.com/time/specials/2007/article/0,28804,1649060_1649046_1649030,00.html |access-date=2025-08-26 |magazine=Time |language=en-US |issn=0040-781X}} in [[Bulandshahr]], [[United Provinces of Agra and Oudh|United Provinces]], [[British India]].{{Cite web |last=Radhakrishnan-Swami |first=Meenakshi |date=14 June 2013 |title=Building on a dream |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/management/building-on-a-dream-105032201044_1.html |access-date=7 January 2025 |website=Business Standard |archive-date=5 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200605022639/https://www.business-standard.com/article/management/building-on-a-dream-105032201044_1.html |url-status=live }} His father, Mukhtar Singh, was a reputed lawyer in Bulandshahr. He completed his schooling at [[Mayo College]], [[Ajmer]].{{cn|date=November 2025}} Later he graduated in science from [[Meerut College]], [[Uttar Pradesh]], he pursued [[Aerospace engineering|aeronautical engineering]] in London, England.{{Cite web |last=IANS |date=15 November 2011 |title=K.P. Singh almost sold DLF stake for Rs 26 lakh |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/kushal-pal-singh-dlf-book-release-25248-2011-11-15 |access-date=7 January 2025 |website=Business Today |language=en}} Singh's uncle was in charge of the [[Stable|stables]] at the then-Viceregal Lodge, which is now [[Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi|Rashtrapati Bhavan]], and during Singh's visit to his uncle, he unexpectedly met the then-[[Governor-General of India|Viceroy of India]], [[Archibald Wavell, 1st Earl Wavell|Lord Wavell]], who suggested he pursue [[Equestrianism|riding]].{{Cite web |last=Mail Today |date=20 November 2011 |title=Mysteries of fate in a splendid life |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/north/story/dlf-chairman-k-p-singh-writes-autobiography-146313-2011-11-19 |access-date=7 January 2025 |website=India Today |language=en}} His father then sent him to [[England]], hiding from Singh that he incurred financial debt to get him there. Singh completed his early education in India and went on to graduate in science from Meerut College. Following his graduation, he moved to the [[United Kingdom]], where he studied [[aeronautical engineering]].{{Cite web |date=2025-04-22 |title=Meet KP Singh, brain behind super expensive DLF Camellias flats in Gurugram, it is home to Shark Tank judges like Aman Gupta, Ashneer Grover, Peyush Bansal and others |url=https://www.india.com/business/meet-kp-singh-brain-behind-super-expensive-dlf-camellias-flats-in-gurugram-it-is-home-to-shark-tank-judges-like-aman-gupta-ashneer-grover-peyush-bansal-and-others-7771324/ |access-date=2025-08-26 |website=India.com |language=en}} While playing [[polo]] in near Windsor, Singh met an officer of the [[Indian Army]] who attempted to convince him to join a [[cavalry]] unit in the army. According to Singh, he was torn between settling in London with a woman named Julie or pursue a military career in India; however, after being allowed to take the [[Indian Military Academy]] entrance exam in England, and later the [[Government of India|Indian government]] agreeing to pay for his journey back to India, Singh decided to join the army. He was later [[Officer (armed forces)|commissioned]] into the [[9th Horse (Deccan Horse)|Deccan Horse]] [[regiment]].{{Cite web |last=Roy |first=Vijay C. |date=1 December 2024 |title=Making of a business leader |url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/book-reviews/making-of-a-business-leader/ |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=The Tribune |language=en}} In 1954, as an army officer, Singh led the Deccan Horse in the 1954 [[Republic Day (India)|Republic Day]] [[Delhi Republic Day parade|parade]]. Singh later resigned from the army, stating that he wanted to work with his father-in-law, [[Chaudhary Raghvendra Singh]], in his company, [[DLF (company)|DLF]], which was then known as Delhi Land & Finance and was founded in 1946.{{Cite news |last=Basu |first=Soma |date=29 November 2024 |title=K.P. Singh: Think like Edwin Lutyens |url=https://www.thehindu.com/real-estate/real-estate-baron-kp-singh-of-dlf-says-visionary-collaborations-and-urgent-action-plans-are-imperative-to-save-our-cities-from-falling-into-a-deeper-chaos/article68914218.ece |access-date=9 January 2024 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} == Business career == === Early career and growth of DLF === After resigning from the army, Singh, together with another retired army officer, initially entered the [[stud farm]] business. He also started a [[Electric battery|battery]] company; however, the venture was unsuccessful and the losses from sustained from it caused Singh's creditors to take him to court. In 1960, Singh joined American Universal Electric Company and, after its merger with DLF Universal Limited (DLF) in 1979, he took over as the managing director with Chaudhary Raghuvender Singh.{{cite encyclopedia |title=Kushal Pal Singh |encyclopedia=Encyclopædia Britannica |url=http://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/1375135/Kushal-Pal-Singh |access-date=2 September 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140408212316/http://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/1375135/Kushal-Pal-Singh |archive-date=8 April 2014}}{{cite web |title=#8 KP Singh |url=https://www.forbes.com/lists/2008/10/billionaires08_KP-Singh_0UU7.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150817044134/http://www.forbes.com/lists/2008/10/billionaires08_KP-Singh_0UU7.html |archive-date=17 August 2015 |access-date=2 September 2015 |website=Forbes}} However, in 1975, Singh almost sold his shares in DLF for 25 [[Lakh|lakhs]] after a decision made by his father-in-law Chaudhary Raghvendra and apathy regarding the [[real estate]] sector due to [[Bureaucracy|bureaucratic]] [[red tape]], but Singh at the last minute declined to do the transaction, keeping his shares.{{Cite web |last= |date=15 November 2011 |title=K.P. Singh almost severed links with DLF |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/books/k-p-singh-almost-severed-links-with-dlf/story-y6O2yZnpVlm9EYi86e7NQP.html |access-date=9 January 2024 |website=Hindustan Times}} In 1976, the [[Government of India]] introduced the [[Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976]] (ULCRA) to grow low-income housing and set limits for the ownership of vacant [[Urban area|urban land]]. The law received a backlash from people who had already invested in the urban land, including Singh, who took over a dormant DLF to attempt to secure exemptions for investors while studying the city’s limitations. He identified the [[Delhi–Gurgaon Expressway|Old-Gurgaon Road]] as a key link between [[Delhi]]'s southern area and [[Haryana]], that had not passed the ULCRA. DLF used the relaxed land acquisition laws as Singh revitalized the company, starting with its 30 acres and rapidly acquiring land from local landowners and farmers. During the 1980s, Singh had a chance meeting with [[Rajiv Gandhi]], who had then just entered politics and later became [[Prime Minister of India]], after his car engine had overheated near Singh's property in Haryana.{{Cite web |last=Rajappa |first=Sam |date=2 November 2012 |title=DLF chief has credited his success in realty business to Rajiv Gandhi |url=https://www.theweekendleader.com/Culture/1393/a-family-enterprise.html |access-date=10 January 2025 |website=The Weekend Leader |language=English}} Singh met Rajiv and spoke about business plans for [[Gurgaon]] and how certain laws were hindering his acquisition of land in the state. Singh later had meetings with Rajiv, and Rajiv convinced his mother, then Indian prime minister [[Indira Gandhi]], to change the Haryana land laws. DLF then received a license to develop land in 1981 and in 1983, the company received another license. During the early growth of DLF in the 1980s, Singh had a dispute with [[Bansi Lal]], a senior politician who had also served as the [[List of chief ministers of Haryana|Chief Minister of Haryana]].{{Cite web |last=Kirpal |first=Raman |date=11 October 2012 |title=Gandhi-DLF link: It all started with Rajiv, not Robert Vadra |url=https://www.firstpost.com/politics/gandhi-dlf-link-it-all-started-with-rajiv-not-robert-vadra-487786.html |access-date=12 January 2025 |website=Firstpost |language=en-us |archive-date=24 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241124154536/https://www.firstpost.com/politics/gandhi-dlf-link-it-all-started-with-rajiv-not-robert-vadra-487786.html |url-status=live }} Lal attempted to ruin Singh's business and even have him arrested, which led to Singh going into hiding on the advice then-Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.{{Cite web |last=Kapoor |first=Coomi |date=10 December 2011 |title=Ultimate Realty Show |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/news-archive/web/ultimate-realty-show/ |access-date=12 January 2025 |website=The Indian Express |language=en |archive-date=6 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171206083409/http://indianexpress.com/article/news-archive/web/ultimate-realty-show/ |url-status=live }} Lal also managed to persuade other Haryana politicians to go against Singh. However, Singh's friendship with Rajiv Gandhi eventually led to Lal stopping his attacks on Singh due to pressure from Rajiv Gandhi. === Established DLF === By the 1990s, several large foreign companies, including [[American Express]], [[British Airways]], [[IBM]], and [[Nestlé|Nestle]] became tenants of DLF properties due to the growth in outsourcing.{{Cite web |last=PTI |date=4 June 2020 |title=DLF's K.P. Singh retires, wishes he turned Gurgaon into the city he dreamed of |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/dlf-s-k-p-singh-retires-wishes-he-turned-gurgaon-into-the-city-he-dreamed-of-11591282377174.html |access-date=12 January 2025 |website=Mint |archive-date=23 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240723124041/https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/dlf-s-k-p-singh-retires-wishes-he-turned-gurgaon-into-the-city-he-dreamed-of-11591282377174.html |url-status=live }} In 1995, Singh become chairmen of the company.{{Cite web |last=Dutta |first=Arnab |date=5 June 2020 |title=DLF's K P Singh retires at 90, son Rajiv Singh to take over reins |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/dlf-s-k-p-singh-retires-at-90-son-rajiv-singh-to-take-over-reins-120060500065_1.html |access-date=15 January 2025 |website=Business Standard |archive-date=15 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211015144319/https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/dlf-s-k-p-singh-retires-at-90-son-rajiv-singh-to-take-over-reins-120060500065_1.html |url-status=live }} Singh constructed numerous earthquake-proof office buildings, apartments, shopping malls and leisure facilities in Gurgaon. While he was the chairman of DLF, the company went for an [[initial public offering]] (IPO) in 2007 and made approximately US$2.24 billion, one of the largest IPOs in Indian history. [[Market capitalization]] of the company in 2007 increased to $24.5 billion, making Singh and his family one of the richest clans in the world.[http://www.time.com/time/specials/2007/article/0,28804,1649060_1649046_1649030-1,00.html/] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071109114641/http://www.time.com/time/specials/2007/article/0%2C28804%2C1649060_1649046_1649030-1%2C00.html/|date=9 November 2007}} In the same year, Singh's [[Cyber City Gurgaon]] was awarded the world’s first [[LEED]] Platinum City and Community Certification.{{Cite web |title=K. P. Singh |url=https://www.ey.com/en_in/entrepreneur-of-the-year/winners-2022/k-p-singh |access-date=2025-01-12 |website=EY |language=en-IN |archive-date=25 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240725155545/https://www.ey.com/en_in/entrepreneur-of-the-year/winners-2022/k-p-singh |url-status=live }} By 2015, Singh scaled DLF's [[Land banking|land bank]] to 10,000 [[Acre|acres]], the largest in India.{{Cite web |last=Srivastava |first=Samar |date=16 November 2015 |title=DLF: The Ailing Giant |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/india-rich-list-2015/dlf-the-ailing-giant/41357/1 |access-date=13 January 2025 |website=Forbes India |language=en}} In 2020, Singh retired from all of his executive positions in DLF, and he was succeeded as chairman of the company his son, Rajiv Singh.{{Cite web |last=BW Online Bureau |date=5 June 2020 |title=DLF's Chairman K.P. Singh Retires At 90, Son Rajiv Singh Takes Over |url=https://bwpeople.in/article/dlf%E2%80%99s-chairman-kp-singh-retires-at-90-son-rajiv-singh-takes-over-194424 |access-date=13 January 2025 |website=BW People |language=en}} === Other business activities === Singh was also one of the initiators for [[General Electric]]’s (GE) entry into India during the 1980s.{{Cite news |last=PTI |date=17 November 2024 |title=When DLF's K P Singh fulfilled Rajiv Gandhi's wish of bringing GE to India! |url=https://www.livemint.com/news/india/when-dlf-s-k-p-singh-fulfilled-rajiv-gandhi-s-wish-of-bringing-ge-to-india-11731841715123.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241120064629/https://www.livemint.com/news/india/when-dlf-s-k-p-singh-fulfilled-rajiv-gandhi-s-wish-of-bringing-ge-to-india-11731841715123.html |archive-date=20 November 2024 |access-date=6 January 2024 |work=Mint |language=en |url-status=live }} His initial work with GE involved bringing their [[Gas turbine|gas turbines]] to India for infrastructure projects and later expanded to advising GE in other industries. Singh also had a key role in establishing India’s first inter-state [[Natural gas|gas]] [[pipeline]] project, the HBJ ([[Hazira]], [[Vijaipur|Bijeypur]], [[Jagdishpur (Industrial Area)|Jagdishpur]]) who was accused of corruption by then-[[Political movement|political activist]] [[Arvind Kejriwal]], who later became the [[List of chief ministers of Delhi|Chief Minister of Delhi]].{{Cite web |last=Banerjea |first=Aparna |date=23 February 2024 |title='You should have politicians as friends and not business partners': DLF's KP Singh |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/you-should-have-politicians-as-friends-and-not-business-partners-dlfs-kp-singh-10156321.html#google_vignette |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207203233/https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/you-should-have-politicians-as-friends-and-not-business-partners-dlfs-kp-singh-10156321.html#google_vignette |archive-date=7 December 2024 |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en-US |url-status=live }} Kejriwal accused Singh of doing a real estate transaction which heavily favored Vadra in return for political favors. In 2023, the [[Government of Haryana|Haryana government]] stated in the [[Punjab and Haryana High Court]] that there were no violations of rules or regulations in the real estate deal between Vadra and DLF.{{Cite web |last=PTI |date=21 April 2023 |title=Haryana says no violation of rules in Robert Vadra-DLF land deal |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/real-estate/haryana-says-no-violation-of-rules-in-robert-vadra-dlf-land-deal-16462221.htm |access-date=13 January 2025 |website=CNBC TV18 |language=en |archive-date=24 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230424001649/https://www.cnbctv18.com/real-estate/haryana-says-no-violation-of-rules-in-robert-vadra-dlf-land-deal-16462221.htm |url-status=live }} === SEBI sanctions === In 2014, the [[Securities and Exchange Board of India]] (SEBI) banned Singh, DLF and 6 others from accessing [[Capital market|capital markets]] for a period of three years due to three violations, non-disclosure of related party transactions, non-disclosure of financial details related to subsidiaries, and inadequate disclosure of outstanding litigation during DLF's 2007 IPO process.{{Cite news |last1=Laskar |first1=Anirudh |last2=Nandy |first2=Madhurima |date=2014-10-13 |title=Sebi bars DLF, KP Singh from capital markets for 3 years |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/TmtlIoJJYlT5X513ZxEiKI/Sebi-bars-DLF-from-capital-markets-for-3-years.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230225085332/https://www.livemint.com/Companies/TmtlIoJJYlT5X513ZxEiKI/Sebi-bars-DLF-from-capital-markets-for-3-years.html |archive-date=25 February 2023 |access-date=2025-01-13 |work=Mint |language=en |url-status=live }} In 2015, SEBI also imposed a heavy fine on Singh, DLF and others; however, DLF appealed SEBI's ruling and the case as of 2019, is in the [[Supreme Court of India]].{{Cite web |last= |date=22 August 2019 |title=DLF stock dips 20% as SC issues notice on non-disclosure |url=https://realty.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/industry/dlf-stock-dips-20-as-sc-issues-notice-on-non-disclosure/70787578 |access-date=13 January 2024 |website=ETRealty.com |language=en |archive-date=29 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220529093257/https://realty.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/industry/dlf-stock-dips-20-as-sc-issues-notice-on-non-disclosure/70787578 |url-status=live }} === Panama Papers === In April 2016, Singh's name featured in the list of high-profile names released in the [[Panama Papers]], a set of 11.5 million confidential documents created by the Mossack Fonseca. Singh's son Rajiv, wife Indira, daughter Pia and her husband Timmy Sarna all set up offshore companies in the [[British Virgin Islands]] through Mossack Fonseca, and are named in the Panama Papers.{{cite web |date=4 April 2016 |title=$10 mn as capital: 10 members of KP Singh's DLF family, three BVI firms |url=http://indianexpress.com/article/india/india-news-india/panama-papers-dlf-panama-papers-k-p-singh-10-million-as-capital-10-members-of-dlf-family-three-bvi-firms/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906230152/http://indianexpress.com/article/india/india-news-india/panama-papers-dlf-panama-papers-k-p-singh-10-million-as-capital-10-members-of-dlf-family-three-bvi-firms/ |archive-date=6 September 2017 |access-date=6 September 2017 |website=Indian Express}} == Personal life and family== Singh was married to Indira Singh, the daughter of Raghvendra Singh, the founder of DLF. Indira died of [[cancer]] in 2018.{{Cite web |date=27 February 2023 |title='She keeps me on my toes': DLF chairman KP Singh finds love again at 91 |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/dlf-chairman-kushal-pal-singh-finds-love-again-91-years-after-wife-die-2340378-2023-02-27 |access-date=13 January 2025 |website=India Today |language=en |archive-date=19 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319171331/https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/dlf-chairman-kushal-pal-singh-finds-love-again-91-years-after-wife-die-2340378-2023-02-27 |url-status=live }} Singh has one son, [[Rajiv Singh]], and two daughters, Renuka Talwar and Pia Singh.{{cite web|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/north/story/whatever-the-odds-corporate-legend-k-p-singh-146317-2011-11-19|title=Whatever the Odds: The candid story of corporate legend K. P. Singh|work=India Today|date=20 November 2011 |access-date=2 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003015318/http://indiatoday.intoday.in/story/whatever-the-odds-corporate-legend-k.-p.-singh/1/160796.html|archive-date=3 October 2015|url-status=live}} In 2023, Singh stated in an interview that he is in a romantic relationship. Singh's son, Rajiv, succeeded him as the chairman of DLF in 2020.{{Cite web|last=Bahree|first=Megha|title=Son Of Property Baron Kushal Pal Singh Succeeds His Father As Chairman Of DLF|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/meghabahree/2020/10/07/son-of-property-baron-kushal-pal-singh-succeeds-his-father-as-chairman-of-dlf/|access-date=2021-05-19|website=Forbes|language=en|archive-date=4 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210504140759/https://www.forbes.com/sites/meghabahree/2020/10/07/son-of-property-baron-kushal-pal-singh-succeeds-his-father-as-chairman-of-dlf/|url-status=live}} Rajiv's wife Kavita Singh became an advisor to DLF Commercial Developers Ltd in November 2002. She was also appointed Advisor to DLF Universal on 1 June 2011, with a retainership fee of Rs 250,000 per month and other benefits. Rajiv and Kavita have two daughters, both of whom work for the company.{{cite web|url=http://businesstoday.intoday.in/story/kp-singhs-grandson-joins-dlf-as-trainee/1/16926.html|title=KP Singh's grandson joins DLF as trainee|website=Business Today|date=11 July 2011 |access-date=2 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140730214155/http://businesstoday.intoday.in/story/kp-singhs-grandson-joins-dlf-as-trainee/1/16926.html|archive-date=30 July 2014|url-status=live}} K.P. Singh's elder daughter Renuka is married to G.S. Talwar, a non-executive director at DLF. Their son, Rahul, has joined DLF India Ltd as a "senior management trainee." K.P. Singh's younger daughter Pia Singh is a full-time director with DLF. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{PadmaBhushanAwardRecipients 2010–19}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Singh, Kushal Pal}} [[Category:1931 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Indian chief executives]] [[Category:Indian billionaires]] [[Category:People from Bulandshahr]] [[Category:People from Gurgaon]] [[Category:Recipients of the Padma Bhushan in trade and industry]] [[Category:People named in the Panama Papers]] [[Category:Indian businesspeople in the real estate industry]] [[Category:20th-century Indian businesspeople]] [[Category:Businesspeople from Uttar Pradesh]]

Kushal Pal Singh (born 15 August 1931) is an Indian billionaire  real estate developer and retired military officer.
He is one of India's richest people according to Forbes.  Singh was the chairman and chief executive officer of the Indian real estate company DLF, founded by his father-in-law Chaudhary Raghvendra Singh, until 2020. Singh built DLF into the largest real estate company in India and DLF holds India's largest land bank of more than 10,000 acres. His autobiography, named Whatever the Odds: The Incredible Story Behind DLF, was published in 2011; Jack Welch spoke at the launch. 
Singh has been noted for making Gurgaon, Haryana, from a village into a modern and developed city. Singh has also been noted for his relationship with the Nehru-Gandhi political family, which, according to him, benefited his businesses especially during its early stages, and has also been a source of controversy during his career. In October 2024, Singh was ranked 12th on the Forbes list of India's 100 richest, with a net worth of $20.5 billion.
